label: SCG I.44 instrumental priority and contingent-effect source scope (#1747)
summary: On the same necessary-root n, informed rational mover h, easy-rescue obligation, claimant standing and norm priority from the #1747 comparison, added fixed CausesOrSustains(n,h) and tested four JavaScript Boolean assignments. With InstrumentOf(h,n) false, all fixed base facts and Aquinas SCG I.44 §4's conditional no-intellectual-instrument-under-unintellectual-principal rule hold while HasIntellect(n) is false; mere causal ancestry is therefore insufficient in this valuation (InstrumentOf is an independent atom here). InstrumentOf(h,n) true with HasIntellect(n) false violates the substantive priority rule. InstrumentOf(h,n) true plus HasIntellect(n) true satisfies it whether or not n actually adopts the selected moral end, isolating actual authorship as distinct. A separate schematic two-world nondeterministic allowed-output relation holds n and the law fixed while outcomes differ, blocking a bare necessity-of-source ⇒ necessity-of-token inference without deterministic completeness; it does not explain the realized token or establish a metaphysically adequate chance source and explicitly reuses #1570/#1730. An independent semantic challenge accepted the conditional inference and located the OPEN purposive-instrumentality warrant. These are finite JS scope/omission controls, not registered Lean, new moral facts, or rival defeats. Primary source: SCG I.44 §4, Latin at corpusthomisticum.org/scg1044.html. Note: docs/notes/moral-governance-intellect-will.md.
blocker: No independent support yet that the rational secondary agent's moral judgment is an instrument of n's own understood and legitimately authoritative end, rather than causally enabled by n while recognizing impersonal norms. To reach the exact existing GodHasIntellect/GodHasWill consumers, also verify same-witness IsGod/necessary-root adapters and distinguish capacity from intentional actual promulgation. Full contrastive explanations of contingent tokens remain #1570/#1459's jurisdiction. No new premise status or formal theorem follows.
